original_query: select     s_store_name   ,s_company_id   ,s_street_number   ,s_street_name   ,s_street_type   ,s_suite_number   ,s_city   ,s_county   ,s_state   ,s_zip   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 30 ) then 1 else 0 end)  as "30 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk > 30) and                  (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 60) then 1 else 0 end )  as "31-60 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk > 60) and                  (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 90) then 1 else 0 end)  as "61-90 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk > 90) and                  (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 120) then 1 else 0 end)  as "91-120 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk  > 120) then 1 else 0 end)  as ">120 days" from    store_sales   ,store_returns   ,store   ,date_dim d1   ,date_dim d2 where     d2.d_year = 2002 and d2.d_moy  = 8 and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk and ss_sold_date_sk   = d1.d_date_sk and sr_returned_date_sk   = d2.d_date_sk and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk and ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and d1.d_date between (d2.d_date - interval '120' day)                and d2.d_date group by    s_store_name   ,s_company_id   ,s_street_number   ,s_street_name   ,s_street_type   ,s_suite_number   ,s_city   ,s_county   ,s_state   ,s_zip order by s_store_name         ,s_company_id         ,s_street_number         ,s_street_name         ,s_street_type         ,s_suite_number         ,s_city         ,s_county         ,s_state         ,s_zip limit 100;
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip,
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.days_diff <= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "30 days",
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.days_diff > 30 AND r.days_diff <= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "31-60 days",
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.days_diff > 60 AND r.days_diff <= 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "61-90 days",
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.days_diff > 90 AND r.days_diff <= 120 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "91-120 days",
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.days_diff > 120 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ">120 days"
FROM (
    SELECT
        ss.ss_store_sk,
        sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk AS days_diff
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d2
      ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
     AND d2.d_year = 2002
     AND d2.d_moy = 8
    JOIN store_sales ss
      ON ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
     AND ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
     AND ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
     AND ss.ss_sold_date_sk BETWEEN sr.sr_returned_date_sk - 120 AND sr.sr_returned_date_sk
) r
JOIN store s
  ON r.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
GROUP BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
ORDER BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate the redundant join to date_dim d1. The condition d1.d_date between d2.d_date - 120 days and d2.d_date, combined with ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk and sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk, is equivalent to ss_sold_date_sk BETWEEN sr_returned_date_sk - 120 AND sr_returned_date_sk (the query itself already uses date_sk subtraction for the day buckets, confirming date_sk differences equal days). This removes a per-row index lookup into date_dim for every qualifying sale-return pair.

Compute sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk once as days_diff in a derived table instead of repeating the subtraction in all five CASE expressions, and push the store join outside the aggregation since store is small (102 rows) and only contributes grouping attributes.
Convert implicit comma-join syntax to explicit INNER JOIN with ON clauses, moving the d2 year/month filter into the join condition so the date_dim scan is pruned before joining store_returns.

Use a single derived table to pre-join store_returns (filtered by August 2002 via d2), store_sales (with the 120-day range pushed into the join condition), and compute days_diff, enabling single-pass conditional aggregation.
